title: Cure Amount for a Suspended Parking License
content:
Collections standard for the Parking License: the cure amount.

## Clause

The cure amount is what a resident pays toward a suspended license so that its privileges can be restored. A payment is applied to the oldest open parking charge first, and the credits and payments already posted on the license always count in full. The cure amount is the whole parking balance of the license, rounded half up to the cent.

## The whole parking balance

The whole parking balance is the license's outstanding parking balance: every charge posted on the license — monthly fees, activation and service fees, EV charging and idle fee lines, fines — less every credit (charge reversal and storage bundle discount credits) and every payment posted on it. Each credit and each payment counts at its full amount.

## Worked example (hypothetical ledger of a suspended license)

| Line | Amount |
|---|---|
| Monthly fee, 1 March | $95.00 |
| Monthly fee, 1 April | $95.00 |
| Violation fine, 12 April | $50.00 |
| Monthly fee, 1 May | $95.00 |
| Charge reversal credit | $12.00 |
| Payment received | $60.00 |

Charges total $335.00; less the credit of $12.00 and the payment of $60.00, the whole parking balance is $263.00, and the cure amount is $263.00.

Applied oldest first, the $60.00 payment goes to the 1 March fee; whichever charges it pays, the credit and the payment count in full against the balance.
